To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the measures of the satisfaction of each of the 1st 4 needs in Maslow’s hierarchy of needs (i.e., physiological, safety-security, and belongingness) were found to be valid, reliable, and able to predict the satisfaction of the next higher need in the hierarchy.

the satisfaction of the 5 basic needs in Maslow’s motivational hierarchy is a reliable and valid construct and that the satisfaction of one need in the hierarchy statistically predicts the satisfaction of the next higher-order need.

(1) Maslow's hierarchy of needs was confirmed by the data; (2) all 5 needs scales were found to be reliable, valid, and useful; (3) the satisfaction of each lower-level need predicted the satisfaction of the next higher need; and (4) family support, traditional value, life satisfaction, and anxiety/worry had significant correlations with the satisfaction level of all 5 of the needs in Maslow’s hierarchy of needs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new measures of the satisfaction of each of the five needs in Maslow’s hierarchy.
the measurement of the satisfaction of each of Maslow's five needs, which are the building blocks of the motivation hierarchy.
the satisfaction of needs as they are defined by Maslow, and we found that Maslow's theory is a good model for predicting satisfaction of higher-level needs from satisfaction of lower-level needs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Maslow motivational hierarchy of needs is supported by these findings.
the Maslow hierarchy of needs is a valid model of human needs, and that the needs are satisfied in a hierarchical fashion.
Maslow's hierarchy is supported by this study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our measures provide a reliable and valid way to assess the level of satisfaction of each need in Maslow's hierarchy.
our measures of the satisfaction of each of Maslow's five needs were psychometrically strong and that the satisfaction of the needs in the hierarchy were positively correlated, as expected.
the satisfaction of a need is a good predictor of the satisfaction of the next higher level in Maslow's hierarchy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the satisfaction of lower-level needs is a necessary but insufficient condition for the satisfaction of higher-level needs, and that the satisfaction of higher needs is a necessary condition for the satisfaction and growth of lower needs. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
